title: Precise, realistic regression assertions

Write tests that pin down the exact behavior under test instead of a loose approximation, and prefer exercising real implementations over mocks that can diverge from production.

- Assert the actual invariant, not a weak bound. If a cost/count should be flat regardless of input size, assert equality across inputs (e.g. `estimate("A".repeat(500_000))` equals `estimate("A")`) rather than only checking it's "much less than" a naive estimate. When a parser must match another implementation's rules, use that implementation as the oracle directly (or property-test against it with many generated inputs) rather than hand-copying its logic into a second parser that can quietly drift.
- Prefer real execution to brittle mocking. Don't mock `child_process`, filesystems, or other OS primitives if doing so would require reimplementing behavior you can't faithfully fake (e.g. symlink resolution, process counts). Run the real command/script against a temp fixture (including platform edge cases: Windows paths, proxy env vars, filenames with glob metacharacters) and assert on the real outcome instead.
- Every bug fix should land with a regression test that specifically fails without the fix and passes with it — pin the exact scenario (a stale cap, a reordered cursor, a dropped failure record) rather than only re-asserting general correctness.
- Assert at the level that actually matters: wire-level request bodies (not just that a code path was hit), exact module-evaluation/call counts for lazy-loading or caching logic, and the exact fields named in a validation error — not just that validation failed.
- Keep tests focused on a feature's core behavioral promises; prune redundant cases that only re-verify implementation details already covered by other tests (e.g. a run-loop's own telemetry/error plumbing), so the suite stays a signal of correctness rather than incidental coverage.

Example, replacing a weak bound with the real invariant:
```ts
it("charges a flat cost per image, independent of payload length", () => {
  const estimate = (data: string) => estimateTokens({ data });
  expect(estimate("A".repeat(500_000))).toBe(estimate("A"));
});
```
